answers.text: Nothing changed. I ran out of days.
Someone needed the day more than I did.
I stopped wanting it and didn't notice.

questions.text: Who did you think of first, this morning?

answers.text: Someone out there in the cold.
No one. I just got up.

questions.text: Was it worth what it cost you?

answers.text: No. But I'd do it again.
I don't know what it cost.
Nothing costs anything here. It all comes back.

questions.text: Could you still say their name?

answers.text: Does it matter, if the day starts over?

questions.text: Tomorrow you'll have the same hours. Same order?

breaks.text: Aldo had the shop, and the debt, and a daughter on the coast. You had a word with his creditor. You gained a morning. He lost the forty years behind that counter, and the coast he was going to see. That one is finished now. It does not start again tomorrow.

self: You had the same day, every day, and you spent it on yourself.
That is not nothing — you were owed a life too.
But the town went on around you, and it went on without you in it.
others: You had the same day, every day, and you gave it away.
It cost you. You can see what it cost you.
They kept what you gave them; that part did not start over.
